Backend pytest: 32 PASS / 1 SKIP (wireless-security no rows to redact — expected) in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration12.py, 33 tests total. Frontend: admin login + Overview live traffic eyebrow shows 'BANDWIDTH TELEMETRY · LIVE FROM ROUTEROS' with real values (7.57 Mbps ↓ / 8.20 Mbps ↑) + Router workspace + Traffic panel with table/chart/Pause + Files→Backups schedule form + Alarms 'Alarm rules' modal (data-testid alarm-settings, cpu_threshold=80) + Edit router modal ssh_port prefilled (1622 — real router listens on 1622, not 22) + Terminal (SSH) actually opened a real session (state=open) since port 1622 is open. Regression: login rate-limit lockout now correctly returns 429 through the public URL (previous iteration's action item is FIXED). Real router mr-65920574 credentials/host/port untouched; ssh_port toggled 22→2222→restored during test.

minor.issue: Real router returns 200 with an empty list (RouterOS has no security-profile rows) so 'redacted' cannot be exercised via this router; pytest skipped that assertion.

ui_bugs.issue: Uncaught runtime error 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading dimensions)' at xterm Viewport._innerRefresh when the user leaves the Terminal (SSH) menu (e.g., clicks Files/Backups) while a session is open. Root cause: SshTerminal.jsx line 23 schedules a setTimeout(fit.fit, 30) that is never cleared on unmount, and the ResizeObserver callback can also fire once more after term.dispose(). Both paths hit the disposed viewport. Cannot switch tabs cleanly without triggering the react-dev-overlay error banner (production may hide the banner but the underlying exception is real and future xterm versions may throw harder).

Bridge Ports → Add: data-testid cfg-bridge stays stuck on the disabled <option>loading from router…</option> even though bridge fetch completes. Suspected: useReferences() sets state undefined→list only on success — if the resource returns an empty items array, the option is replaced but the disabled attribute may remain because list.length===0 falls through the '—' render path. In this run cfg-interface loaded correctly (73 options) but cfg-bridge did not populate. Repro: open Bridge Ports → Add, wait 8s.
React DOM warning 'In HTML, <option> cannot be a child of <span>' triggered near App.js line 228. Minor invalid nesting, no visual impact but pollutes the console.

issues: Recharts still logs two 'width(-1)/height(-1)' warnings during first render before the container measures — cosmetic (same as iteration 11).

action_items: SshTerminal.jsx: clear the 30ms setTimeout(fit.fit) and stop the ResizeObserver *before* calling term.dispose() in the effect cleanup, so switching menus while an SSH session is open doesn't throw. Suggested: const fitTimer = setTimeout(...); return () => { clearTimeout(fitTimer); observer.disconnect(); ... term.dispose(); }.

ConfigEditor useReferences: when the reference endpoint responds with 200 but items=[], render an enabled empty <select> (or the fallback text input) instead of leaving the disabled 'loading from router…' option — currently Bridge Ports > cfg-bridge is unusable if the router has no bridge yet.
App.js line ~228: fix invalid <option> nested inside <span> HTML to silence the hydration warning.
critical_code_review_comments: engine.py sample_interfaces filters by kind.startswith(PHYSICAL_PREFIXES) then totals() sums only UPLINK_PREFIXES — VLAN/bridge are captured but excluded from totals, correct per requirement.

engine.py cron_ack uses asyncio.create_task(job) without keeping a reference; the task can be garbage-collected before it finishes (Python 3.11 warns about this). Consider stashing tasks in a module-level set and discarding on done_callback.

sshterm.py _open_shell uses AutoAddPolicy (no host key verification) — acceptable for a management console over a private network but should be documented. Also invoke_shell timeout is 0.2s + a busy-wait via asyncio.to_thread(_read); this is fine functionally but pins one worker thread per active session — capacity risk if many operators open shells simultaneously.
server.py write_config sets body.values = {} when command == 'remove' AFTER the KEY_RE/length validation loop that already ran over the (unused) values — validation gate is misleading (harmless).

server.py deliver_alarm swallows every telegram send exception with 'continue' — if a role's token is malformed nothing surfaces to the operator; consider logging the failure into alarm_log so audit shows attempted-but-failed deliveries.

engine.py scan_alarms writes last_scan_at only into workspaces present in cache — a workspace with no reachable routers never gets its 'last_scan_at' timestamp updated. Fine but confusing when the UI shows 'not run yet' forever.
server.py grew to 585 lines; engine.py is 315; sshterm.py is 83. Splitting server.py into resources/writes/telegram/backups is overdue.
engine.py backup_schedules 'weekday' field is stored/consumed but the UI only shows it for weekly frequency — schedule_public still exposes weekday for daily rows (cosmetic).

SshTerminal.jsx re-opens the WebSocket whenever `attempt` changes — that also happens when the user just tab-focuses the button because setState is called synchronously; nothing debounces it. Not a real bug today but easy to abuse.

rca_of_the_issue: SshTerminal.jsx effect installs a setTimeout(30ms) for fit.fit() AND a ResizeObserver on holder.current, then registers a cleanup that calls observer.disconnect(); keys.dispose(); socket.close(); term.dispose(). Order is wrong for two reasons: (a) the setTimeout is not stored so it cannot be cleared — if it fires between socket.close() and term.dispose() the fit runs against a still-live term but a detaching DOM node, and if it fires just after term.dispose() the addon hits `undefined.dimensions`; (b) the ResizeObserver keeps a reference to the DOM node; the moment React unmounts the ws-menu the observer fires one final callback which invokes fit.fit() -> Viewport._innerRefresh on a disposed terminal. Mitigation: store the timer id, clear it in cleanup, and disconnect the ResizeObserver BEFORE term.dispose(); guard fit.fit() with a `disposed` flag.
